question: Do corrected white-paper labels beneath ink and two additional reviewed checker scenes improve material identity and usable full-pipeline results under corrected family grouping?

protocol.encoder: Same pretrained frozen parameters and BatchNorm statistics; train decoder and material head.
protocol.modelSelection: Fixed final update, no held-out tuning.
protocol.groupingCorrection: The verified ordinary checker with printed heart decoration belongs with checkers, not the framed-motif group. Both arms use this correction. Existing source/duplicate groups and historical reports are unchanged.

evaluation: Independently audit checkpoints, frozen encoder, source hashes and held-out membership.

Evaluate both arms on identical current nineteen-instance labels; report shared seventeen and two new scenes separately. Baseline models for the new scenes come from the checkpoint held out on the same checker family.
Require exact synthetic-control tensors and shared predictions where training data/schedules are unchanged. The checker-held-out model has the same six training motifs in both arms.
Report full body IoU, observed material error, missing-body joint error and per-material balance; partial interior accuracy does not establish usable boundaries.
Inspect all nineteen predictions and rerun complete crop/fitting/editable checks for both learned arms and the existing pipeline. No claim of improved recovery from pixel scores alone.
limitations: Previously inspected development photos, one seed and two broad source/motif folds. No unseen-test or physical-assembly claim.
This combined data intervention does not isolate the label correction from the two new scenes; follow-up isolation is required if a useful improvement appears.
No ONNX model, application integration, push or deployment.
